ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The problem gives that in triangle ABC, A=30°, C=105°, b=4. First find the third angle: B=180°-A-C=180°-30°-105°=45°. According to the standard notation for triangles, side a corresponds to angle A, and side b corresponds to angle B. By the sine rule, a/sin A = b/sin B; substituting gives a = 4·sin30°/sin45° = 4·(1/2)/(√2/2) = 2√2. Therefore a=2√2.

method.method_draft: Use the sine rule directly. Read the givens A=30°, C=105°, and side b=4. First compute the remaining angle B=180°-30°-105°=45°. method.method_draft: Use a geometric altitude decomposition. Read A=30°, C=105°, b=AC=4. Compute B=45°. Drop the perpendicular from A to the line BC, meeting the extension of BC beyond C at D because C is obtuse. In right triangle ACD, AC=4 is the hypotenuse and the acute angle at C is 180°-105°=75°, so AD=4sin75° and CD=4cos75°. In right triangle ABD, angle B=45°, so it is a 45-45-90 triangle and BD=AD. Since D lies beyond C, BD=BC+CD=a+CD. Thus a=AD-CD=4(sin75°-cos75°)=4·(√2/2)=2√2.
